method: Independent lens review of captured evidence. The director opened every screenshot for a surface before scoring it, read the axe and capture results, and scored without sight of any other director's scores.
overallNote: The governing fact of this review is that my lens is motion, feedback and delight, and the evidence is fourteen still frames. Transitions, easing, hover and focus states, drag behaviour on the board, optimistic updates on Mark done, skeleton and loading states, toast entrances, the voice-capture recording experience, and whatever the About spine and the Timeline countdown do on scroll or load are all entirely unobserved. Unobserved is unproven, so no surface here scores as if that half went well — the ceiling on this baseline is what the resting frame demonstrates, and nothing above roughly 8 was reachable regardless of how good the motion turns out to be. What the stills do show is a product with a genuine and above-average feedback vocabulary at rest: written empty states rather than blanks ("Nothing held up", "No conversation yet. Comments and changes will appear here as they happen."), status carried in words as well as colour, provenance closed back to source in Notes, keyboard hints surfaced as chips, and a clear single commit action per layer. Against that sit three concrete, verifiable defects: the notification layer is unanchored and lands on live controls (it covers the Keep / Turn into task / Delete row on mobile Notes and cuts two rows in the desktop task list — confirmed by crop), the mobile task detail has no scrim, no handle and a clipped grey element half off the top edge so it reads as a page rather than a layer, and the mobile board's column chips carry no selected state for the gesture they exist to serve. Marketing scores lowest here not on craft but on inertness — landing, about and pricing each open with a screen offering nearly nothing to act on, and pricing in particular gives an arriving user no control at all. All ten axe runs returned zero violations, all captures were HTTP 200 with no console errors, which is clean but says nothing about my lens. No vetoes: the banner occlusion is the closest call, but it is review-mode chrome in a review-mode capture and calling it disqualifying for release would be wrong even though the layering flaw it exposes is real. This baseline should be re-run against motion capture — short screen recordings of drag, mark-done, save-note, sheet open and the countdown — before anyone treats these numbers as a settled read on this lens.

surfaces.rationale: Resting-state feedback vocabulary is real: per-column orientation copy ("In motion right now.", "Held by a reply, a delivery, or a decision."), count chips, a written empty state ("Nothing held up" in a proper card, "No tasks in this group" in list), completion shown as green tick plus tinted card fill, and a header ledger ("5 of 13 complete", "1 overdue", "Day 11 of 97", "5 undated"). Three defects my lens can actually see. First, the toast layer has no content offset: the "In development. You're seeing it early." pill sits bottom-centre over live content and, cropped at 2x, visibly cuts the descenders of "Chase linen order, now shipping Tuesday" and covers "before the date" on the row beneath it in the desktop list. That is review-mode chrome, but it proves the toast slot is unanchored, so every real toast will occlude rows the same way. Second, the mobile column chips (To do 3 / In progress 3 / Review 2 / Waiting 0, with a fifth peeking) are five identical grey outlines with no selected or current state, so nothing feeds back which column the horizontally scrolling board is showing — the primary mobile navigation gesture has no state indicator, and the chip row just clips at the edge with no fade mask. Third and largest: drag-and-drop is the defining interaction of a board and the stills carry zero evidence of it — no grab affordance, no drop-target styling, no lift treatment — and I give it no credit. Overdue urgency ("Overdue by 2 days" red, "Due today" amber) is carried by colour plus wording, which is fine, but the card's only commit affordance is an unlabelled circle whose hover, focus and toggle transition I cannot observe.
surfaces.highestLeverageFix: Anchor the toast/banner layer to a reserved safe area that offsets board and list content instead of floating over rows, and give the mobile column chips a real selected state bound to board scroll position.

surfaces.rationale: This is the most feedback-literate surface in the app. The coach-mark "Press e to open a task full-screen, and j or k to move between tasks." with its own dismiss, the return-key chip sitting beside "Draft a reply", and the anticipatory empty state "No conversation yet. Comments and changes will appear here as they happen." are all deliberate — the last one tells the user what future feedback will look like before any exists, which is genuinely good practice. The header cluster (up/down chevrons, expand, overflow, close) plus a single indigo "Mark done" gives one obvious commit action against a properly dimmed desktop scrim, so the modal reads as a layer. Mobile is where it falls down. There is no scrim at all, no drag handle and no grabber, so the sheet reads as a page rather than a layer and the only dismiss affordance is a small x. Cropping the top edge at 3x confirms a light grey rounded element clipped by y=0 directly above the "The Orch… / T-1" breadcrumb, with no legible purpose — either a mispositioned parent-peek or an artifact, and either way the entry and dismiss story on mobile is not readable from the resting frame. The keyboard coach-mark, the one explicit delight beat, is desktop-only with no mobile substitute. Everything my lens most wants to judge here — the open transition, whether "Mark done" animates or optimistically updates, what "Make copies" and "Doesn't repeat" do when pressed — is invisible in stills, so I score the observable half only.
surfaces.highestLeverageFix: Give the mobile detail a real sheet identity — dimmed backdrop, visible drag handle, drag-to-dismiss — and fix the clipped grey element at the top edge so the layer reads as a layer rather than a page.

surfaces.rationale: The capture loop is visibly instrumented. "Write the thought before it disappears…" is the best microcopy in the product and does feedback work by naming the cost of inaction. Type/Voice/Photo is a segmented control with an actual indigo active state — one of the few unambiguous selected states anywhere in these captures — and the capture mode is fed back into the list as per-row icons (text, mic, image). Triage is inline and legible: Keep / Turn into task / Delete with the destructive in red, "To review" and "In Tasks" pills, a left indigo rule plus tint on the selected row, and a footer that closes the loop with "Captured 35 minutes ago · Edited 31 minutes ago" and a live link to the derived task. Against that: the banner physically covers the Keep / Turn into task / Delete row on mobile — I cropped it at 3x and the pill's opaque body sits across all three labels — so the toast layer occludes precisely the controls this surface exists to offer. "Save note" is the weakest-weighted control on the page: a pale grey outline with grey label, lighter than the Type toggle beside it, carrying no shortcut hint even though the product clearly has a hint vocabulary (the "/" chip sits in the search field two rows below). The reading pane leaves roughly 450px of dead space under a three-line note with no affordance in it. And voice capture — the one place where recording state, waveform and transcription progress are the entire experience — is wholly unevidenced, so I credit none of it.
surfaces.highestLeverageFix: Stop the notification layer landing on the Keep / Turn into task / Delete row on mobile, and promote "Save note" to a real primary with a visible enabled/disabled transition and a keyboard hint.

surfaces.rationale: The most delight-forward surface here, and the state vocabulary on the axis is genuinely considered: filled dots for complete, hollow for future, an indigo filled dot for the next milestone, a "Today" tick, labels alternating above and below the rail (Complete / Our next milestone / Later / Coming up), "2 of 9 complete" under the countdown, and "Live since 15 Jul 2026. Anyone holding the link can read it." as plain-language sharing-state feedback rather than an icon. The 79 / days countdown at desktop is a real moment. But my lens has to be blunt about what stills withhold. The countdown is the single element that most obviously wants motion — a count-up, a tick, anything on load — and I have no way to know whether it has any, so it earns nothing on that axis. The "4 milestones" cluster is plainly an expand interaction carrying almost no affordance: a hairline bracket and a caption, no chevron, no button treatment, nothing that says press me. On mobile the countdown drops from roughly 110px to 40px, so the biggest delight beat is largely surrendered on the viewport where a couple planning a wedding will actually open the link. The Timeline / Milestones / Preview / Share cluster reads ambiguously — Milestones carries the filled grey while the timeline view is what is shown — so the segmented state is fighting itself. Substantial dead band between hero and axis at desktop as well.
surfaces.highestLeverageFix: Give the "4 milestones" cluster a real affordance and expand behaviour, and carry the countdown's scale and moment through to mobile rather than shrinking it to a caption.

surfaces.rationale: Above the fold there are exactly two interactive elements, and both carry a directional glyph — "See the system at work ↓" and "Join the waitlist →" — which is the right instinct, since the arrow tells you what the click will do before you do it. The mono eyebrow "NOTES → TASKS → TIMELINE" is a quiet, well-judged beat and the single indigo "outside" gives the headline one point of colour emphasis. That is the whole of what my lens can verify. Everything else it cares about is unavailable: whether the ↓ smooth-scrolls or jumps, whether the NOTES → TASKS → TIMELINE chain animates, whether anything reveals on scroll, what "Products ⌄" does when opened. More pointedly, the first screen is entirely static type with no product imagery, no device frame, no loop — nothing that stands in for motion or demonstrates that the system feels calm when it moves. A page whose promise is a calm system in use opens with a wall of type and two buttons. The desktop hero also leaves the entire right half empty and around 200px of dead space beneath the eyebrow before the fold, so the composition gives motion nowhere to live even if it exists below.
surfaces.highestLeverageFix: Put one piece of live product evidence above the fold — a real Notes-to-Tasks moment in motion — so the hero demonstrates the system rather than asserting it.

surfaces.rationale: The indigo spine running down the left margin with a filled dot at its head — and, on mobile, a hollow square node further down the same rule — is a deliberate motif that strongly implies scroll-linked progression tied to the founder's argument. It is the right idea, and I can see exactly none of it working, so I credit the intent and nothing of the execution. Beyond that motif, the first screen carries zero interactive elements other than the nav: no CTA, no next step, nothing to act on, no affordance whose feedback I could assess. The desktop capture leaves the entire lower-left quadrant blank beneath "…by tech companies, for tech companies." with the body paragraph isolated in the right column, which at this viewport reads as a page caught mid-assembly rather than a resolved composition — and because I cannot rule out that this is a reveal-on-scroll state captured mid-flight, I have to score the frame I was actually given rather than the one I might charitably assume. Mobile resolves better, stacking headline over body with the spine intact and the node visible. The typography is strong and the argument lands, but my lens is feedback on action and deliberate delight, and this surface offers almost no action to feed back on.
surfaces.highestLeverageFix: Resolve the desktop composition so the founder's note reads as finished at rest, and make the indigo spine's scroll progression legible in a still frame rather than only in motion.

surfaces.rationale: The first screen of the surface a user reaches specifically in order to act contains no actionable control at all — no plan card, no CTA, no billing toggle, nothing but the headline, the subhead, and a three-cell fact strip. That is the core finding for my lens: momentum arrives at this page and the page gives it nowhere to go. The strip itself (No charge / on the waitlist, VAT included / at the prevailing rate, Terms repeated / before purchase) is good pre-emptive reassurance and "Anything unresolved is named plainly" is honest, but static reassurance is standing in for the live control a pricing page normally needs, and I have no evidence such a control exists anywhere, let alone how it responds. The one piece of visual rhythm on the screen is also off: the first cell runs from the viewport edge to roughly 533px while the other two are about 373px each, so the divider spacing is unequal and the strip reads as misaligned rather than measured. "Choose by the work in front of you." implies a comparison interaction below the fold that the capture cannot reach. Mobile stacks the strip cleanly into three rules, which works better than desktop.
surfaces.highestLeverageFix: Bring an actionable control above the fold — plan selection or at minimum the primary CTA — and even out the fact-strip cell widths so the one rhythmic element on the screen holds.
